newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm near record, trend up - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm near record, trend up - traders.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed throughout Thursday, closing near record highs on news U.S. authorities had approved LUKoil preferred share ADRs.
Traders said the rally would probably continue on Friday.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose 1.25 percent to 310.63 from 306.79 on Wednesday and close to Wednesday's record high of 312.66.
Market volume was a healthy $46.2 million, but traders said the market would firm more on Friday due to the absence of Western or local sellers.

Oil company LUKoil announced the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission had approved American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) for its preferred shares and traders said interest was strong in both LUKoil and Surgutneftegaz oil company shares.

"We thought Surgutneftegaz preferreds would follow on the LUKoil preferreds' coat-tails," said Andrei Kukk, head of Rinaco Plus' corporate stock division. "We though that ordinaries would follow the preferreds."
Prices on LUKoil preferreds rose to $12.60 from $11.75 at the close on Wednesday, while Surgutneftegaz prefs rose to $0.463 from $0.430.
LUKoil ordinaries rose to $15.42 from $15.10 and Surgutneftegaz ordinaries rose to $0.635 from $0.602.
Traders said the price of the LUKoil prefs ADRs, which represent two underlying shares, was about $25-$26.
